description: Adapt frontend for Railway deployment: configurable API URL via VITE_API_URL, Railway-specific nginx config without proxy_pass, updated Dockerfile for Railway, and railway.json
steps: 1. Edit frontend/src/lib/api.ts: Change baseURL from hardcoded '/api' to 'import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || "/api"'. This allows Railway to set VITE_API_URL at build time to point to the backend service URL.

2. Create frontend/nginx.railway.conf: A Railway-specific nginx config that does NOT have the proxy_pass /api/ block. It should: listen on port 80, serve static files from /usr/share/nginx/html, have SPA fallback (try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html), and cache static assets.

3. Update frontend/Dockerfile: Add a build ARG for VITE_API_URL so Railway can pass it at build time. In the build stage, set ENV VITE_API_URL from the ARG. For the production stage, use nginx.railway.conf instead of nginx.conf (or make it configurable). Since the local docker-compose still needs the proxy nginx.conf, create a Dockerfile.railway that uses nginx.railway.conf, OR modify the existing Dockerfile to accept a build arg for which nginx conf to use.
4. Create frontend/railway.json with Railway service configuration: specify how to build (Docker), pass VITE_API_URL as build arg.
5. Verify: run 'cd /projects/sandbox/contable/frontend && npm install && npm run build' to confirm the frontend compiles without errors.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/nginx.railway.conf exists with SPA routing but NO proxy_pass to backend
frontend/railway.json exists with proper Railway config
Frontend builds without TypeScript or Vite errors
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/contable/frontend && npm install && npm run build
findings: All changes verified. Frontend builds without errors. VITE_API_URL is configurable via build arg for Railway. nginx.railway.conf has no proxy_pass. Dockerfile defaults to nginx.railway.conf for Railway, docker-compose overrides to nginx.conf for local dev.
